name: Pregabalin + Methylcobalamin
meta: Pregabalin: Gabapentinoid (neuropathic pain / anxiolytic / antiepileptic); Methylcobalamin: Active vitamin B12 coenzyme (neurotrophic)
Prescription-only fixed-dose combination. Components – Pregabalin: Schedule H –
prescription only; Methylcobalamin: Prescription combination ingredient
sections: White to off-white crystalline solid, freely soluble in water.
Cobalamin (corrinoid) – methyl coenzyme form of vitamin B12
Bright red crystals or crystalline powder; light-sensitive.

Pregabalin: Developed as a more potent successor to gabapentin; pain relief may begin within the first week. First approval/introduction: Synthesised 1990 (Richard B. Silverman, Northwestern University); EU and US FDA 2004 (Pfizer). Methylcobalamin: One of the two active coenzyme forms of vitamin B12 (with adenosylcobalamin), used widely in India and Japan for peripheral neuropathy. First approval/introduction: Mecobalamin approved in Japan (Eisai) for peripheral neuropathy.
Pregabalin provides symptomatic neuropathic pain relief; methylcobalamin supports nerve regeneration and myelination, addressing nerve repair as well as pain.

Pregabalin Binds the alpha-2-delta subunit of voltage-gated calcium channels with higher affinity than gabapentin, decreasing release of excitatory neurotransmitters; analgesic, anxiolytic and anticonvulsant. Receptor / target profile: Binds the alpha-2-delta-1 protein of voltage-gated calcium channels with high affinity, reducing release of glutamate, norepinephrine and substance P.

Methylcobalamin Coenzyme for methionine synthase; promotes myelin and nucleic-acid synthesis, axonal regeneration and remyelination of damaged peripheral nerves; reduces homocysteine. Receptor / target profile: Cofactor for methionine synthase; promotes myelin and axonal protein synthesis.
Summary: Bioavailability ≥90% (linear); Tmax ~1 h. Not protein bound; negligible metabolism. Half-life ~6.3 h. Renally excreted unchanged – adjust dose to CrCl.
Oral ~1–2% by passive diffusion at high doses; intrinsic-factor-mediated absorption
Summary: Absorbed via intrinsic factor and passive diffusion; stored in liver; excreted in urine and bile.
Post-herpetic neuralgia and other peripheral neuropathies
Neuropathic pain associated with vitamin B12 deficiency (e.g. long-term metformin use)
One capsule once or twice daily as directed
Adjust pregabalin dose in renal impairment
Dose to be individualised by the treating physician according to clinical response and tolerability.
CrCl ≥60: 150–600 mg/day; 30–60: 75–300; 15–30: 25–150; <15: 25–75 mg/day; supplement after dialysis.
Peripheral oedema – caution in heart failure
Metformin, PPIs, colchicine reduce B12 absorption
Pregabalin: With or without food; avoid alcohol.
Pregabalin: Renal function; weight; oedema; misuse; respiratory status.
Pregabalin: Somnolence, confusion, agitation, restlessness, seizures (rare), coma. Supportive care; haemodialysis effective. Methylcobalamin: Very low toxicity.
Evidence derives from component trials; methylcobalamin trials in diabetic neuropathy (largely Asian) report modest symptom improvement.
Dizziness, drowsiness and weight gain may occur
Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light and moisture. Keep out of the reach of children. Do not use after the expiry date.
